title: Question 14709
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Question ID: 14709_paul_pen_picnic
Transformed from: 14709

At a Christian law-school picnic, Timothy, a student assistant, often admired Professor Paul’s engraved fountain pen and frequently said that he wished he had one like it. Paul decided to give Timothy the pen for Timothy’s birthday the following week.

During the picnic, Paul took the pen out of his shirt pocket and left it on a blanket when he went to join a volleyball game. Timothy walked by, saw the pen on the blanket, and decided to steal it. He bent over and picked up the pen. Before he could put it into his backpack, Paul returned. Seeing Timothy holding the pen, Paul said, “I know how much you like that pen. I was planning to give it to you for your birthday. Go ahead and take it now.” Timothy kept the pen.

Timothy has committed
rightExplanation:
A is correct.

Gold Key: Larceny completes when the actor takes possession without consent, intends to steal, and moves the property even slightly. Later permission does not erase the completed taking.

Silver Key: In a larceny-versus-attempt pair, stop grading the labels and find the movement fact. Here, Timothy picked up the pen before Paul gave permission.

Timothy decided to steal the pen before Paul spoke. He picked it up from Paul’s blanket. That is the taking and slight movement. Paul’s later birthday-gift permission came after the crime had already completed.

c3.label: CUT
c3.text:
* C is cut as the wrong theft frame. The stem never gives Timothy lawful possession before conversion.
* D is cut after the theft-clock anchor: later permission does not erase the earlier unauthorized taking.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text:
* A and B clash on one axis: completed taking versus mere attempt.
* Splitting fact: Timothy picked up the pen before permission.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text:
* Gold Key resolves the axis: slight movement completes larceny.
* Residual answer: A.

studentScript: A/B is the fight. Did the object move before permission? Yes: Timothy picked it up. Gold Key says slight movement completes larceny. C needs prior lawful possession. D loses because later permission came too late. Pick A.

A.signal: Matches the A/B movement axis after applying the slight-movement Gold Key.
A.lawyer: Common-law larceny is a trespassory taking and carrying away of another's personal property with intent to permanently deprive; slight movement is enough.

B.signal: It answers an incomplete-taking case. The stem gives a completed pickup before permission.
B.lawyer: Attempt is displaced by the completed larceny once taking and slight asportation occur.

C.signal: It would fit a later conversion after lawful possession. The stem gives no prior entrustment.
C.lawyer: Embezzlement requires lawful possession or entrustment before wrongful conversion.

D.signal: It treats the later gift as if it erased the earlier unauthorized pickup.
D.lawyer: Later consent does not undo the completed trespassory taking with intent to steal.

goldKeys.statement: Larceny completes when the defendant takes possession without consent, intends to steal, and moves the property even slightly; later permission does not undo it.
goldKeys.trigger: The actor picks up the item before the owner gives permission.
goldKeys.authority: Common-law larceny; People v. Davis; Robinson v. United States

goldKeys.statement: Embezzlement requires prior lawful possession or entrustment; a first unauthorized taking from the owner’s possession is the larceny frame.
goldKeys.trigger: The answer choice says embezzlement but the stem never entrusts the item to the actor before the taking.
goldKeys.authority: Common-law theft distinction; Georgia theft annotations on embezzlement/lawful possession

remediation.title: Theft Clock: Unauthorized Pickup Locks the Crime
remediation.signal: Later permission appears after an unauthorized pickup.
remediation.studentMove: Put a line between the pickup and the later permission. Decide the crime at the pickup.
remediation.tinyRule: If intent to steal exists before the unauthorized pickup, slight movement completes larceny.
remediation.trap: Choosing attempted larceny or no crime because the owner later consented.
